llm.summary: The skill is a real brainstorming workflow, but it automatically hands project context to other skills/subagents and edits planning files without a clear approval gate.

dimensions.detail: Writing docs/project-brief.md, saving .attune/brainstorm-session.json, passing all brainstorming context to another skill, dispatching a subagent, and having the main agent revise the spec are high-agency behaviors for a brainstorming skill unless the user expects that orchestration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is markdown-only with no executable installer, hooks, package scripts, or install-time code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It uses broad triggers such as planning and requirements, and explicitly says not to prompt before continuing into the next phase after writing the brief.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates persistent project and session files, but shows no privilege escalation, credential access, background daemon, destructive action, or hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose is coherent, but the skill goes beyond brainstorming by requiring War Room deliberation, automated review, and automatic continuation into project specification.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your brainstorming may include private business plans, internal constraints, or sensitive stakeholder details. Use standalone or stop-after-brainstorming options when you only want a brief, and check generated files before allowing downstream specification work.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The War Room handoff is disclosed and adjacent to decision quality, but mandatory transfer of all brainstorming context to another skill expands authority beyond simple ideation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The automatic continuation into project specification is documented, but the no-confirmation handoff reduces user control after the brainstorming output is saved.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Multi-LLM deliberation may fit advanced planning, but making it required and passing full context is broader than necessary for a basic brainstorming aid.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The triggers planning and requirements can invoke this workflow in generic project contexts where the user may not expect automatic orchestration and file writes.
[SQP-2] expected: Creating docs/project-brief.md is expected for this skill, but users should know it can write local project artifacts.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Cross-skill sharing is disclosed in the body, but there is no clear opt-in warning before all brainstorming context is passed onward.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The spec-review loop lets the main agent apply fixes during review iterations, which is quality-gate behavior but can silently change requirements.
[EA2] unexpected: The instruction not to prompt before continuing is artifact-backed and materially weakens user oversight for chained skill execution and file modification.
